record.notes: The communiqué is dated 26 August 2026, Sydney, and was published on GOV.UK by the Home Office on 28 August 2026. Outside its section on AI and national security, it notes that state threats are amplified by advanced technology including AI, that AI gives terrorists and violent extremists new tools for radicalisation, propaganda, attack planning and fundraising, and that the fast-growing threat of online and cyber-enabled scams is largely driven by AI-enabled technology. It does not set out which model characteristics may require additional government scrutiny.

verification.note: Stored and read in this run: the GOV.UK HTML communiqué and its publication page (Home Office policy paper, published 28 August 2026). They confirm the title, the Sydney meeting of 25-26 August 2026, the 26 August 2026 dateline, the participating ministers and the full text of the AI and national security section. Other host-government copies were not stored. The previous note's report, from a commentary seen in search results, that none of the five governments had released the scrutiny criteria rests on no stored source.

status.quote: We, the Home Affairs, Interior and Security Ministers of Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and the United States (the ‘Five Countries’) convened under Australia’s Chairmanship, in Sydney on 25-26 August 2026, for the Five Country Ministerial (FCM).
